title: Longest Block With Equally Many 0s and 1s

concept.title: Turn the zeros into minus ones
body: A block with the same number of 0s and 1s becomes a block with sum 0 if every **0 is counted as -1**. Then the longest balanced block is the longest block whose prefix sums at both ends are equal. Store the first position of every prefix sum.
The trick "replace one kind of element by -1 so that balance means sum zero" is useful for all questions that compare two counts inside a block.

statement: Given an array of 0s and 1s, find the length of the longest block of consecutive elements that contains the same number of 0s and 1s. If there is none, print 0.
inputFormat: The second line has `n` numbers, each 0 or 1.

examples.note: The whole array has three 0s and three 1s.

hints: Count a 0 as -1 and a 1 as +1.
A balanced block has the same balance at its two ends.
Store the first position of each balance value.

explanation: With 0 counted as -1, balanced blocks are the blocks between two equal prefix balances; the earliest occurrence gives the longest one.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

first = {0: -1}
balance = 0
best = 0
for i in range(n):
    balance += 1 if a[i] == 1 else -1
    if balance in first:
        best = max(best, i - first[balance])
    else:
        first[balance] = i
print(best)
